findings.title: Hash and parse the retained response from the same captured bytes
findings.problem: validate_capture_result hashes the body, reads it again for JSON parsing, and hashes it a third time for its reference. A transient change during only the parser read can therefore enter flat while references and origin attest the original raw SHA. The earlier whole-manifest check does not bind the later parser read, and no later body-to-flat identity check rejects the returned mismatch.
findings.impact: The new one-shot original operation can consume a URL that was not in the accepted response bytes while its provenance still cites those accepted bytes. Same host, same book and source page_index16 do not reject the changed basename. Worker/download reachability beyond the pure URL gate is static reasoning; no worker, source_stage, Store, adapter or download was executed for this counterexample.
findings.classification: Inherited helper pattern exposed at the new retained-reuse contract; no retroactive reversal of actual04 finite acceptance.
findings.minimum_repair: Read each body once into raw; verify its byte length and digest and perform duplicate-key/nonfinite-rejecting JSON parsing on that same raw. Derive references/origin from that same verified digest. A later digest alone cannot reject a transient replacement restored before the digest.
